name: Optic Nerve Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Reduced diameter of the optic nerve head on fundoscopic examination
Presence of visual impairment or decreased visual acuity consistent with optic nerve underdevelopment
MRI evidence of optic nerve hypoplasia and associated midline brain abnormalities
Exclusion of other causes of optic nerve atrophy or hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of reduced optic nerve head size on fundoscopic exam plus visual impairment consistent with optic nerve hypoplasia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Neuroimaging is supportive but not mandatory; diagnosis is clinical with ophthalmologic confirmation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Optic disc pallor with reduced diameter
Visual acuity reduction consistent with optic nerve underdevelopment

laboratory: Hormonal assays showing pituitary hormone deficiencies (e.g., GH, TSH, ACTH)
imaging: MRI showing reduced optic nerve size
Midline brain abnormalities such as absence of septum pellucidum or corpus callosum hypoplasia
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; mostly sporadic cases
other: Fundoscopic examination revealing small, pale optic discs

distinguishingFeatures: Optic nerve atrophy is acquired rather than congenital
History of optic nerve injury or disease
Acute or subacute vision loss in young adults
Central vision loss with characteristic mitochondrial DNA mutations

redFlags: Signs of pituitary hormone deficiency (e.g., hypoglycemia, growth failure)
references: Johns Hopkins Medicine. Optic Nerve Hypoplasia Overview.
Miller NR. Optic Nerve Hypoplasia. In: Walsh & Hoyt’s Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology. 6th ed. 2005.
Orphanet: Optic Nerve Hypoplasia. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 2012.
